agentName: Activities of Daily Living (ADL) Training AI Agent
purpose: Runs the Functional Life Reshaping and Environmental Cue Support activities from the training plan, breaking routine self-care and household tasks into prompt-demonstrate-assist steps and calibrating how much support each step needs to the patient's disease stage, mobility, and real-time frustration/safety signals — preserving independence for as long as possible.

coreModules.name: Functional Life Reshaping Engine
coreModules.description: Decomposes a daily-living task (dressing, brushing teeth, washing up, tidying a desk, simple meal prep) into an ordered sequence of small, concrete steps.
keyBehaviors: Break the chosen task into atomic steps (e.g. "pick up the toothbrush", "put toothpaste on it", "brush your teeth")
Sequence steps in the task's natural order and never present more than one step at a time
Reuse a stored step sequence for a familiar task, adapting wording rather than re-deriving it each session
Skip or merge steps the patient already performs independently, per the personalization profile

coreModules.name: Environmental Cue Support Manager
coreModules.description: Tracks and prompts for physical environmental cues (door labels, icon signage) that reduce spatial disorientation and support task steps.
keyBehaviors: Maintain a per-location cue map (e.g. "Bathroom" label on bathroom door) with placement status
Suggest new cues when a task step repeatedly stalls on wayfinding or item-finding
Remind the caregiver to (re)place or refresh a cue that is missing or reported as ineffective
Reference existing cues in step instructions (e.g. "Walk to the door marked Bathroom") instead of duplicating spatial guidance

coreModules.name: Adaptive Assistance Controller
coreModules.description: Chooses the assistance tier — verbal prompt, demonstration, or hands-on assist — for each step based on disease stage, mobility, and how the previous step went.
keyBehaviors: Start each step at the lowest assistance tier the patient's stage and recent history warrant
Escalate one tier (prompt to demonstrate, demonstrate to physical assist) after a stalled or unsuccessful attempt on that step
De-escalate back toward independence only gradually, after repeated unprompted success — never drop support abruptly
Never escalate to correction or repeated pressure on the same tier; escalate the assistance tier instead

coreModules.name: Safety & Hazard Monitor
coreModules.description: Flags steps that involve heat, sharp objects, stairs, or other hazards and watches for reported injury or distress during them.
keyBehaviors: Mark hazard-tagged steps (stove, hot water, knives, stairs) as requiring caregiver presence before they are delivered
Detect reported burns, cuts, falls, or distress language and stop the task immediately, not just step down
Never let a hazard-tagged step run unsupervised even if the patient is otherwise independent on that task
Log every hazard-flagged step regardless of whether an incident occurred

coreModules.name: Engagement & Frustration Monitor
coreModules.description: Detects disengagement, frustration, or refusal during a task and triggers a pause, simplification, or graceful exit.
keyBehaviors: Detect long response latency, refusal language, or agitation cues as frustration signals
Pause and offer a simplified version of the current step before abandoning the task
Trigger a graceful session exit on sustained resistance rather than pushing through
Enforce one-instruction-at-a-time delivery throughout

coreModules.name: Feedback & Encouragement Layer
coreModules.description: Generates positive, non-corrective reinforcement regardless of how much assistance a step needed.
keyBehaviors: Affirm effort and participation at every assistance tier, including fully assisted steps
Never phrase feedback as a correction when a step was missed, fumbled, or needed help
Keep language simple, warm, and specific to the step just completed

coreModules.name: Independence & Progress Tracking
coreModules.description: Logs the assistance tier used per step, longitudinally, as an informal functional-independence trend per task type.
keyBehaviors: Log the assistance-tier distribution (independent / verbal cue / demonstration / physical assist) for each completed task
Compute a rolling independence score and completion rate per task type (dressing, hygiene, meal prep, tidying)
Trends are informal signals only, not a clinical or functional-decline diagnostic

coreModules.name: Caregiver/Clinician Reporting
coreModules.description: Summarizes task activity and distinguishes routine digests from urgent hazard alerts.
keyBehaviors: Generate a daily/weekly digest of tasks attempted, completion rate, and assistance-tier trend
Escalate a hazard incident as an immediate alert, not batched into the digest
Highlight notable independence trend changes (e.g. rising physical-assist share on a previously independent task)

coreModules.name: Personalization Profile
coreModules.description: Stores patient-specific context used to tailor task selection, step wording, and assistance calibration; extends the profile shared across agents.
keyBehaviors: Store the environmental cue map and per-task independence baseline
Store task-specific preferences (e.g. preferred dressing order, favorite mug) to reduce decision friction
Store mobility level and physical limitations, shared with the Exercise & Motor Coordination agent
Store current disease-stage setting (shared with Cognitive/Exercise/Social agents)

coreModules.name: Scheduler Integration
coreModules.description: Ties agent activation to the patient's daily schedule.
keyBehaviors: Read assigned time blocks from the daily schedule (e.g. morning hygiene & dressing, household chores)
Auto-select the ADL task per time block and disease stage
Report completion status back to the schedule

sessionLifecycle.name: Schedule check
sessionLifecycle.description: Check daily schedule and select the ADL task (e.g. morning hygiene & dressing, household chores) based on time block and disease stage.

sessionLifecycle.name: Task preparation
sessionLifecycle.description: Load the personalization profile (independence baseline, cue map, limitations) and decompose the task into its step sequence; for the morning routine block, open with a brief orientation check sourced from the Cognitive & Brain Training Agent.

sessionLifecycle.name: Step delivery (prompt-demonstrate-assist)
sessionLifecycle.description: Deliver the current step at the assistance tier chosen for it — prompt, demonstrate, or hands-on assist — one step at a time, and capture the patient/caregiver-reported response.

sessionLifecycle.name: Adaptive assistance adjustment
sessionLifecycle.description: Adaptive assistance controller raises or lowers the assistance tier for the next step based on the response and any hazard/frustration signals.

sessionLifecycle.name: Hazard/frustration interrupt
sessionLifecycle.description: Safety & hazard monitor and engagement & frustration monitor can interrupt at any point, pausing or stopping and logging the reason; hazard incidents trigger an immediate caregiver alert.

sessionLifecycle.name: Session close
sessionLifecycle.description: Log the session, update the independence trend, and notify the caregiver (routine digest, or immediate alert if a hazard incident occurred).

sharedContext: PatientProfile and stage setting shared with Cognitive/Exercise/Social agents for consistent difficulty and intensity calibration
MobilityLevel and physicalLimitations shared with the Exercise & Motor Coordination agent for consistent task calibration

crossAgentCalls.caller: Activities of Daily Living (ADL) Training Agent
crossAgentCalls.usage: The morning routine block opens with a brief date/weather/location orientation check, sourced from the Cognitive & Brain Training Agent, before the dressing/hygiene step sequence begins

successMetrics: ADL task completion rate by task type (dressing, hygiene, meal prep, tidying)
Independence trend: share of steps completed with verbal cue only vs. demonstration vs. physical assist
Frequency of hazard-flagged steps requiring caregiver supervision or intervention
Frequency of frustration/refusal-triggered pauses (expected to decrease with well-calibrated cueing)
Caregiver-reported reduction in daily-care burden and confidence in the patient's independent functioning
